obligations.note: The new payment-advice integration is in the inventory with an empty owner ("") and no purpose, so it lacks a required owner. The exhaustive control test test_integrations_are_inventoried fails with ('payment-advice', 'no owner').
The added integration uses https://advice.fernbrook.example/v1, and the exhaustive control test test_integrations_use_tls passed in the change's CI run.
Ticket CHG-24697 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-14, before review. Its components (payments.controls-data, payments.integrations) cover both changed files.
Mara Costa, a change_approver for payments and not the author (Sofia Santos), gave the code_review approval.
All approvals name the single commit fa3a7a3, which is the head; there are no later commits.

The CI run on head fa3a7a3 has result 'failure' with 2 failing tests, including the registered INV-1 control test. The JUnit report's timestamp (2026-10-23) and its developer-machine hostname also do not match the run record.
integrations.py is in the security-sensitive component payments.integrations. Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
controls/payments/asset-inventory.json is a protected path. Bao Tran (control_owner, controls-office team, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved on the head commit.
The change and its ticket are standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
The change deviates from INV-1, and no exception in the register covers INV-1 or payments.integrations, so the deviation is not acceptable.
No ledger entry covers integrations.py or the asset inventory. The covered code (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Underwriting.java, Policy.java) is unchanged.

summary: The change registers a new NPI-classified integration but leaves its inventory owner empty and omits a purpose. This violates INV-1, and no approved exception covers it. The change's own CI run on the head commit failed, including the registered INV-1 control test, so CHG-4 is not met. The ticket, independent, security and control-owner approvals are all in order, but the violations require rejection.
